title: Karniyarik
subtitle: Turkish baked aubergines stuffed with spiced lamb and pine nuts
excerpt: Aubergines split down the middle and fried until silky, then filled with a fragrant spiced lamb mixture and baked in tomato sauce until tender. A classic Turkish stuffed vegetable dish.
sourceNotes: Classic Turkish home cooking. Karniyarik means split belly, a reference to the way the aubergine is cut. Eaten across Turkey, most often for a midday meal.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made a day ahead. Fry the aubergines and assemble on the day.

content.text: Karniyarik depends on getting the aubergines properly soft before they are stuffed. Fry them in enough oil to colour and collapse them; they will not taste right if they are baked from raw. The lamb filling should be moist but not wet.

items.prepNote: to thin the sauce in the tin

content.text: Peel strips from each aubergine lengthways to create a zebra pattern, leaving some skin on. Cut a deep slit down the length of each aubergine from stalk to tip, without cutting all the way through. Sprinkle the cut sides with salt and leave for 20 minutes. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the aubergines for 4 to 5 minutes per side, turning carefully, until softened and golden. Transfer to the roasting tin.
In the same pan, cook the pine nuts for 1 minute until golden. Set aside. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, green pepper, and tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the lamb mince. Break it up and cook for 6 minutes until browned. Add the diced tomatoes, allspice, cinnamon, and salt. Stir and cook for 4 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down. Stir in the parsley and pine nuts.

Heat the oven to 190C. Press open the slit in each aubergine with a spoon. Spoon the lamb filling generously into each slit, mounding it up slightly. Lay a slice of tomato and a slice of green pepper on top of each.

Mix the passata with the water and pour around the base of the tin. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for 15 minutes more until the tops are lightly coloured. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Older or very large aubergines can be bitter, and the salting step was skipped.
items.fix: Always salt the cut flesh and leave for at least 20 minutes, then pat dry before frying.

items.symptom: The filling spills out during baking.
items.cause: The slit was cut too wide or the aubergine was too soft to hold shape.
items.fix: Press the sides together around the filling before baking and use toothpicks to hold the slit together if needed.

items.symptom: The aubergines are dry after baking.
items.cause: Not enough sauce in the base of the tin.
items.fix: Make sure the passata reaches at least 1cm up the sides of the aubergines before covering with foil.
